carmen: Quick heads-up: found a reproducible race in the Go sample that uses context.Background() + streaming generator. If a token refresh happens while the iterator is active and a handler cancels, the iterator sometimes panics (send on closed channel) or returns duplicate close errors.

leo: Can you paste the minimal repro and logs?

carmen: Minimal snippet (sample uses Background currently):
```go
ctx := context.Background()
g := client.NewGenerator(ctx, client.Opts{Model: "tiny"})
it := g.Stream("hi")
for it.Next() { fmt.Println(it.Value().Text) }
if err := it.Err(); err != nil { log.Println(err) }
```
stack: "panic: send on closed channel" from gen.streamer.push in some runs.

abi: Two problems: 1) Background makes lifecycle ambiguous for request-bound code; 2) our token refresh path can swap token/transport concurrently with active stream goroutines.

leo: Short fixes: update sample to use request ctx (NewGenerator(req.Context(), ...)) and make iterator own teardown (it.Close()) so ownership is clear. Also wrap auth refresh in singleflight/mutex so we don't mutate shared transport mid-stream.

carmen: I'll open a tiny PR that: updates sample to use request ctx, adds a TTL-toggle repro script, and adds an integration test that forces concurrent refresh + cancel with -race.

parity-bot: FYI: open a parity ticket if you change public surface. See PARITY-58.

abi: Also add a short DX doc blurb: "Avoid context.Background() for streaming generators; prefer request-scoped contexts and explicit iterator.Close()."

leo: If we want to evolve the API, consider returning an iterator type with Close() error and keep the old API as shim for compatibility. That reduces surprise about client.Close affecting existing iterators.

carmen: Filing INF-3301 and attaching repro. Will @parity on the PR. Thanks all.
